hook.text: In 2019-2020, Australian fires burned 18.6 million hectares — an area larger than Greece.

buildup.text: Record drought and heat primed the landscape. When fires started, they couldn't be stopped.

discovery.text: Smoke blanketed Sydney for weeks. Air quality was 11 times the hazardous threshold.

twist.text: An estimated 3 billion animals were killed or displaced — the worst wildlife disaster in memory.

climax.text: Some ecosystems that normally recover from fire may not survive this time. The heat was too intense.

punchline.text: Fire is natural in Australia. This fire season was not.

quiz.question: How many animals were affected by Australia's Black Summer fires?

details.summary: Australia's 2019–2020 Black Summer bushfire season burned over 18 million hectares, destroyed 3,000 homes, killed 33 people, and was estimated to have killed 3 billion wild animals. It was fueled by record drought and heat linked to climate change.
details.whyItMatters: Black Summer was unprecedented in scale and shocked a fire-adapted nation. It demonstrated that no level of preparedness is sufficient when climate conditions exceed all historical experience.
takeaways: Over 18 million hectares burned in eastern and southern Australia
An estimated 3 billion animals were killed or displaced
Smoke affected air quality for millions across Australian cities

faq.question: What made Black Summer unprecedented?
faq.answer: Record temperatures, the driest year on record, and drought conditions primed fuels across the continent simultaneously. Fires burned through temperate rainforests that had not burned in thousands of years, reaching a scale never seen in Australia's recorded history.

faq.question: How did Black Summer affect Australian wildlife?
faq.answer: An estimated 3 billion mammals, birds, and reptiles were killed or displaced. Koalas lost roughly 30 percent of their habitat in New South Wales. Species already at risk from habitat loss faced the additional shock of fire across their entire range.
